text:
B: Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yeah. Hiya.
B: I'm Daniel. Worthing.
A: Liam. Walsall.
B: Nice one. I put on the form you looked like you'd just come off a shift. Was I close?
A: Yeah, nights. Four on the bounce. IT at a parcel depot.
B: Ah, right. I'd guessed tradesman, so, half right.
A: Half, yeah. What do you do?
B: Erm, I run the trade counter at a builders' merchant. Half six starts, so I'm sort of the opposite end of the day to you.
A: Half six is alright. I'm usually just finishing then.
B: [laughs] Yeah. How long are your shifts?
A: Twelves. I pick up overtime, so fifty-odd hours a week.
B: That's a lot. I'm about fifty-two with Saturdays, and I'm knackered by Friday. Why so much overtime, if you don't mind me asking?
A: Money. Trying to save for a house. Renting at the minute, me and the wife, in Bloxwich. Want to buy before we have kids, but, er... it's not moving very fast, to be honest.
B: No, I get that. I'm saving for a deposit too. I'm back living with my parents, which at thirty-two is, erm, not where I pictured it.
A: Do you pay them?
B: Rent, yeah. Less than a flat would cost, so it's sort of the sensible thing. My mum still does most of the dinners, so I can't really complain.
A: Free tea. Can't argue with that.
B: That's what my mates say. Is there much you can do to speed it up, the house thing?
A: Bit on the side. I fix broken stuff off Marketplace and sell it on. Graphics cards, controllers, laptops. Got a card last week for ninety, the fan was dead, fiver to fix, it'll go for two-fifty.
B: That's a decent margin.
A: Yeah. People don't know what they've got. They see it not turn on and they just want it gone.
B: We get a bit of that at work, funnily enough. Someone brings back a tool saying it's knackered and it's just the battery.
A: Yeah. Exactly that.
B: Do you ever feel bad, buying it cheap?
A: Not really. They set the price. I'm not robbing anyone.
B: Fair enough. I'm useless at haggling. I'd probably end up paying more than they asked.
A: [laughs] Don't go on Marketplace then.
B: Noted. What would you do if you weren't on nights?
A: Network engineer, days. Doing a CCNA, slowly. Hard to study after a twelve.
B: I know that one. I'm doing an Open University module in the evenings, history. Some nights I just sit there reading the same page.
A: Same. I fall asleep on the settee with the laptop open, wake up and the dog's on top of me.
B: [laughs] What kind of dog?
A: Staffie cross. Diesel. He's chewed the settee cushion again.
B: Ha. My parents had a Labrador who ate a whole loaf once, bag and all.
A: Diesel'd do that. He's done a tennis ball in about ten minutes.
B: Do you think the CCNA will get you off nights, then?
A: Hopefully. Or I'll just move firms. Whoever pays more, really. I'm not fussed about—
